Thirty Years, Three Eras  ·  IWBI 2026 · Era III
SLIDE 1 / 23
Lesion→Image→Patient→Population

From detection to risk.

We're at the brink of Era III — no longer just finding the lesion, but reading the whole image, and the whole patient. The same normal mammogram from the start holds three more things:

1  tissue-based 5-year risk
2  cardiovascular risk (BAC)
3  a recurrence score

We'll come back to the heart (§5) and the tissue (§4). First — risk.

Era III
For forty years, the only risk signal we could read off the image was density — coarse, subjective, and a weak predictor.
Tyrer-Cuzick, Gail, BCSC — questionnaire-and-density models
~0.62
Tyrer-Cuzick v8 · 5-yr AUC
~0.59–0.61
density-augmented Gail / TC
Strong across a population.
Weak for the woman in front of you.
Era III

The image itself carries risk — beyond density.

Yala et al. (Radiology 2019) showed a network reading the image out-predicted the classical models. Mirai (Yala et al., Sci Transl Med 2021) predicts across time points, tolerates missing risk-factor data, and stays consistent across scanners.

C-index 0.76 / 0.81 / 0.79 — US · Sweden · Taiwan
41.5% of future cancers flagged high-risk (vs 22.9% Tyrer-Cuzick)

But a C-index is a black-box number. For a screening program, we have to know why it works.

Yala et al., Radiology 2019 · Mirai — Sci Transl Med 2021 (DOI 10.1126/scitranslmed.aba4373)
Era III
AsymMirai: much of the signal is local bilateral asymmetry.

AsymMirai (Donnelly et al., Radiology 2024 — Duke + Emory, EMBED 210,067 mammograms) reverse-engineered Mirai's signal: the left-vs-right tissue difference. A transparent model on that alone nearly matched the black box — 1-yr AUC 0.79 vs 0.84; 3-yr AUC 0.92 in stable tissue. Performance you can explain is performance you can audit.

Era III

From research model to a cleared product.

Clairity — FDA De Novo authorization, June 2025: the first tool to predict 5-year breast-cancer risk from a routine screening mammogram alone.

validated across ~77,000 mammograms · 5 sites
added to 2026 NCCN screening guidance

Research model to cleared product to guideline in under five years — though there is no primary peer-reviewed validation paper yet.

Clairity — FDA De Novo 2025 · NCCN 2026 (AI-based risk assessment)
Era III

Risk-adapted screening: less for most, more for the few.

WISDOM (Esserman et al., JAMA 2026; 28,372 women) — risk-based screening (gene panel + polygenic score + clinical model → regimens from 6-monthly MRI down to defer) vs annual.

non-inferior for advanced (stage ≥IIB) cancers
~3,800 fewer mammograms /100k person-yr
89% chose risk-based
did not reduce biopsies

NCCN 2026 already recommends MRI at ≥1.7% 5-yr AI risk — practice running ahead of the MIRAI-MRI trial readout.

WISDOM — JAMA 2026;335(9):763–774 · NCCN 2026 · MIRAI-MRI (NCT05968157)
Era III

A maturity gradient: concept → simulation → RCT.

StudyPersonalizesEngineEvidence tier
TEMPO (2022)IntervalImage (Mirai) + RLRetrospective / simulated
Mirai-interval (2025)Supplemental flagImage-basedRetrospective
ScreenTrustMRI (2024)Modality (MRI)Image (AISmartDensity)RCT — secondary endpoint
WISDOM (2025)Interval + start ageClinical + genetic (BCSC+PRS)Pragmatic RCT — primary

The largest RCT evidence (WISDOM) uses genetic/clinical risk; the most sophisticated engines (TEMPO, Mirai) are image-based but untested in a prospective interval RCT. The two haven't met yet — that's the open frontier.

TEMPO: 25% fewer mammograms (Karolinska) · ScreenTrustMRI: AI ~4× more efficient than density (64.4 vs 16.5 cancers /1,000 MRIs) · 30% of high-risk-variant carriers had no family history
Era III · image → patient

The image tells us when to look and how hard.

Once we find something, the question changes: from "is there cancer, and what is her risk?" to "what is this cancer, and what will it do?"

Lesion→Image ✓→Patient →→Population

That answer is on a glass slide. We move to the pathology lab — where AI does something our images cannot.

Lesion→Image→Patient→Population

Across the hospital, in the pathology lab.

So far we have stayed in the reading room. The same arc — hand-built tools, then deep learning, then foundation models — has played out in pathology, and it has one capability our images do not: inferring molecular and genomic features directly from the stained slide.

This is also where the third model from the opening lives — the recurrence score read from a glass slide.

Era III · morphology → molecular (the third model)

Estimating the Oncotype DX recurrence score from the H&E slide.

0.89 vs 0.73
flags high-risk (RS>25) vs a leading nomogram
0.75 vs 0.49
predicts recurrence in low-RS patients — beating the score itself

Oncotype DX costs ~$4,000 and takes 1–2 weeks. Orpheus (6,172 cases, 3 institutions) infers the 21-gene Recurrence Score directly from the H&E. This is what imaging cannot do: morphology → molecular identity.

Boehm et al. ("Orpheus"), Nature Communications 2025 · concept: Kather et al., Nature Cancer 2020
Era III · morphology is molecular

Inferring molecular features from the H&E, including invasive lobular carcinoma.

Invasive lobular carcinoma hides in dense tissue and grows single-file — the hardest cancer to catch on mammography. It is defined molecularly by loss of E-cadherin (the CDH1 gene). A model predicts CDH1 status from the H&E alone. The morphology was always a readout of the biology underneath; it just wasn't visible by eye.

CDH1 from H&E · AUC ~0.94
74% of AI-flagged cases had hidden CDH1 inactivation the assay missed
Cancer Research 2024 (Mount Sinai) · PMID 39106449 — a dedicated model, not Virchow
Era III · pathology's reader study

CAMELYON16: AI compared with pathologists on lymph-node metastasis.

0.994
best algorithm · AUC
0.810
pathologist panel · AUC (under a 2-hour limit)

Lymph-node metastasis on H&E, 11 pathologists under realistic time pressure. Under the clock, the best AI exceeded the panel; top algorithms matched experts given unlimited time. The point is fatigue and time, not replacement.

Ehteshami Bejnordi et al., JAMA 2017 · DOI 10.1001/jama.2017.14585
Era III · a call that now picks a drug

HER2-low: AI improves agreement on the 0-versus-1+ call.

Since trastuzumab deruxtecan (DESTINY-Breast04), HER2-low is treatable. That makes the HER2 0-vs-1+ distinction decisive — a call the assay wasn't designed for, on which pathologists disagree.

pathologist agreement 72.4%
automated AI 92.1%
0-vs-1+ reader agreement 70% → 87%
Krishnamurthy et al., JCO Precision Oncology 2024 · DOI 10.1200/PO.24.00353
Era III · combining the two specialties

Analyzing radiology and pathology together.

Radiology and pathology have been handled as separate departments, with separate images and separate reports. AI now makes it practical to analyze them together for the same patient.

Lesion→Image ✓→Patient →→Population

Radiology AI localizes the lesion; pathology AI infers molecular features from the same disease; multimodal models combine the two. This is what the next section means by clinical intelligence.

Lesion→Image→Patient→Population

The patient, not the pixel.

No single modality sees the whole patient. Mammography, ultrasound, MRI, pathology, the genome — each answers a different question. Fusing them outperforms any one alone.

Era III · multimodal fusion

Fusing the modalities beats any one of them.

Each modality answers a different question — the "risk vector" logic from the risk section, generalized to the whole patient.

PORPOISE: multimodal beat unimodal in 12/14 cancers
breast pCR: multimodal AUC ~0.89 (Joo 2021; Hong 2026)
image partly predicts the molecular profile (Schmauch)

Honest caveat: some multimodal gains reflect dataset batch effects (Howard/Kather/Pearson 2023) — under site-preserved validation the advantage shrinks.

Chen (PORPOISE), Cancer Cell 2022 · Schmauch, Nat Commun 2020 · Joo 2021 / Hong 2026
Era III · multimodal fusion

Fusing the radiology modalities: MG + US + MRI.

Each answers a different question — mammography for calcifications and architecture, ultrasound for the dense breast, MRI for extent. Fusing them improves lesion characterization.

A two-stage MG + US model with modality-specific attention reached AUC ~88% — 13–16 points over either modality alone. Three-tier frameworks now fuse MG + US + MRI + clinical.

Pan/Xu/Fang, J Appl Clin Med Phys 2026 (663 patients). Your group (RSNA 2026): do MG + MRI complement pathology-derived features for pCR? Emerging direction, not trial-level evidence.

+13–16 points from fusion alone
Era III · multimodal fusion

BINDS: staged US/MG → MRI, taught to see like pathology.

A two-stage system mirroring real escalation: US/MG first, then MRI for the comprehensive read.

Radiology–pathology alignment: a pathology encoder (trained on whole-slide images) guides the imaging encoders, so the imaging model learns pathology-relevant features.

27,048 participants · 8 centers + 7 public sets

Nature Biomedical Engineering 2026 (DOI 10.1038/s41551-026-01654-2).

Era III · multimodal fusion

The endpoint: a digital twin of the patient.

Her imaging, pathology, genome, and history fused into one model that updates with every visit — and lets us weigh the consequences of a decision before we make it.

A patient-level model spanning imaging, pathology, and genomics — the concrete form of "the patient, not the pixel."

Sadée et al. (Gevaert, Stanford), Lancet Digital Health 2025 — medical digital twins
Lesion→Image→Patient→Population

The mammogram as a whole-body biosensor.

The same image she came in for holds more than cancer. Breast arterial calcification (BAC) — discarded as an incidental finding for 40 years — is a sex-specific cardiovascular signal that goes unread on millions of mammograms.

BAC → ASCVD HR 1.51, independent of usual risk factors (Iribarren 2022)
Cardiovascular & opportunistic
123,762
women, no known CVD — AI-quantified BAC → cardiovascular risk

Dapamede et al. (Emory + Mayo), European Heart Journal 2026 — the largest to date. A transformer segments BAC and reports burden (mm²) with a continuous, dose-dependent association with MACE and all-cause mortality. Severe BAC → HR ~2.2 (internal) / ~1.8 (external), adding prognostic value on top of the AHA PREVENT score.

Dapamede, Eur Heart J 2026;47(18):2206–2220 · segmentation: Guo et al. (SCU-Net), Med Phys 2021 — your group
Cardiovascular & opportunistic

Beyond the calcium: the whole image predicts cardiovascular risk.

Barraclough et al. (Heart 2026) — DeepSurv on routine mammograms predicts CVD risk in ~49,000 women at C-index ~0.72, comparable to clinical risk equations, without isolating BAC. The tissue itself carries the signal.

Caveats: BAC is not coronary calcium (modest correlation) — an independent marker, not a substitute for CT calcium scoring. And opportunistic predictions need their own prospective validation and a care pathway: a score is useless if no one owns the abnormal result.

Barraclough et al., Heart 2026 (~49,000 women) · BAC vs coronary calcium: Saccenti 2024 (AUC ~0.64)
Cardiovascular & opportunistic

Every image is a richer biosensor than its indication.

Retina → age, sex (AUC 0.97), cardiac events 0.70 (Poplin 2018)
ECG → asymptomatic low EF AUC 0.93 (Attia 2019)
CT → bone density, aortic calcium (Pickhardt 2020)

We can offer tens of millions of women a cardiovascular screen from an image they already came for — at no added cost and no added radiation.

Who gets that capacity, and who is left out, is a question of access and equity — where we go next.
